# DCAT-US 3.0: what reaches RDF, and what does not

Built 2026-09-04 against [GSA/dcat-us](https://github.com/GSA/dcat-us) at `7a6e803`, using rdflib 7.6.0, pySHACL, open-ontologies (Rust engine). Every figure below is regenerated by `make build`; none of them is typed by hand.

## 1. The headline

The same 115 published examples, expanded three ways.

| Expansion | Triples | Distinct predicates | DCAT-namespace triples | Empty files | Processor errors | Invented IRIs |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| As published (no context) | 76 | 1 | 0 | 38 | 1 | 0 |
| Generated binding, faithful to declared ranges | 1,508 | 123 | 228 | 10 | 0 | 98 |
| Generated binding, relaxed where the corpus supplies labels | 1,510 | 123 | 228 | 10 | 0 | 0 |

Reading the first row: the corpus as it stands today yields 76 triples across 115 files, one distinct predicate (`rdf:type`), and no DCAT vocabulary at all. Reading the third: the same files, unchanged, carry 1,510 triples and 228 DCAT statements once a context exists.

The binding that produces rows two and three was not written. It was generated from `jsonschema/definitions/`, which already records an RDF IRI for most properties.

## 2. The schema already contains the binding

| Measure | Count |
| --- | --- |
| Classes defined | 26 |
| Classes declaring `_oldDocs.rdfClass` | 26 |
| Properties defined | 270 |
| Properties declaring `_oldDocs.uri` | 231 |
| Properties with no RDF IRI | 39 |
| Distinct property names across all classes | 119 |

26 of 26 classes and 231 of 270 properties carry the RDF term they stand for, retained from the SHACL definition when it was retired. Publishing a context is therefore not a new source of truth. It is a projection of the existing one, and it can be rebuilt on every commit.

## 3. Where the schema disagrees with itself

4 JSON keys map to more than one RDF property depending on which class they appear in. A context has to resolve each one, which is why generation surfaces them and hand-maintenance does not.

| Key | Majority mapping | Used by | Divergent mapping |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `conformsTo` | `dcterms:conformsTo` | 5 classes | `Document` &rarr; `dcterms:identifier` |
| `mediaType` | `dcat:mediaType` | 1 classes | `Document` &rarr; `dcterms:mediaType` |
| `publisher` | `dcterms:publisher` | 4 classes | `Document` &rarr; `dc:publisher` |
| `title` | `dcterms:title` | 9 classes | `Kind` &rarr; `vcard:title` |

`Kind.title` &rarr; `vcard:title` is correct: on a contact card, a title is a job title. The other three sit in one file, `Document.json`, and read as drift rather than intent. `conformsTo` mapped to `dcterms:identifier` is the clearest case: five other classes map the same key to `dcterms:conformsTo`.

A further 10 keys agree on the IRI but disagree on the declared range or cardinality between classes; they are listed in `build/audit.json` under `shapeConflicts`.

## 4. Properties with no RDF binding

| Class | Unbound | Properties |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Dataset` | 11 | `created`, `first`, `hasCurrentVersion`, `hasPart`, `inventoried`, `previousVersion`, `replaces`, `rightsHolder`, `supportedSchema`, `wasAttributedTo`, `wasUsedBy` |
| `Concept` | 5 | `altLabel`, `definition`, `inScheme`, `notation`, `prefLabel` |
| `Document` | 5 | `accessURL`, `category`, `corporateCreator`, `downloadURL`, `otherIdentifier` |
| `Identifier` | 5 | `creator`, `issued`, `notation`, `schemaAgency`, `version` |
| `Distribution` | 3 | `availability`, `inventoried`, `otherIdentifier` |
| `Location` | 3 | `altLabel`, `otherIdentifier`, `prefLabel` |
| `Catalog` | 2 | `datasetSeries`, `otherIdentifier` |
| `DataService` | 2 | `inventoried`, `otherIdentifier` |
| `Standard` | 2 | `category`, `otherIdentifier` |
| `Agent` | 1 | `category` |

`Concept` and `Identifier` are the notable entries: every property they declare is unbound, so neither class can be given a shape at all, and between them they are the most frequently instantiated objects in the example corpus. `prefLabel`, `altLabel`, `definition`, `inScheme` and `notation` on a `skos:Concept` have obvious SKOS equivalents; nothing in the repository records them.

## 5. Values that cannot reach RDF

22 keys are declared with a resource range and published with a plain label instead, 100 times across 7 files. Under a faithful context each of those labels is resolved against the base IRI, producing 98 triples whose object is an identifier that exists nowhere else in the world. JSON Schema cannot see this: the value is a string, and a string is what it expects.

| Key | Occurrences | Published values |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `accessRights` | 6 | `Public access with no restrictions`, `Public access with no restrictions. Data is freely available for download and use.` |
| `accrualPeriodicity` | 7 | `daily`, `quarterly` |
| `algorithm` | 5 | `SHA-256` |
| `category` | 1 | `Organization` |
| `compressFormat` | 1 | `application/gzip` |
| `format` | 8 | `CSV`, `JSON` |
| `geometry` | 3 | `POLYGON((-125 24, -66 24, -66 50, -125 50, -125 24))` |
| `hadRole` | 12 | `Data Steward`, `isInputTo` |
| `inDimension` | 1 | `height` |
| `language` | 10 | `en`, `es` |
| `liabilityStatement` | 2 | `This dataset is provided as-is without warranty of any kind. Users are responsible for determining fitness for their intended use.`, `This dataset is provided as-is without warranty. The publishing agency is not liable for any damages arising from its use.` |
| `mediaType` | 12 | `application/pdf`, `text/csv` |
| `packageFormat` | 1 | `application/zip` |
| `provenance` | 3 | `Data collected from automated weather stations deployed at 2,500 locations across the continental United States.`, `Quality control procedures applied according to WMO guidelines.` |
| `relation` | 1 | `some resource` |
| `restrictionStatus` | 4 | `Restricted` |
| `rights` | 9 | `This data is in the public domain and may be used without restriction.`, `This catalog is maintained by the Federal Data Management Office.` |
| `source` | 1 | `Original metadata harvested from NOAA data portal` |
| `status` | 1 | `published` |
| `tel` | 7 | `+1-555-123-4567`, `+1-555-CLIMATE` |
| `theme` | 1 | `Climate Science` |
| `unitMeasure` | 4 | `percent` |

Some of these are ordinary vocabulary gaps: `language: "en"` wants an IRI from a language register, `mediaType: "text/csv"` wants an IANA media type IRI. Others are more serious. `accessRights`, `rights`, `provenance` and `liabilityStatement` are whole sentences declared with the range of a statement resource, so a faithful expansion turns a paragraph of English into an identifier.

## 6. The deleted shapes were never given anything to validate

| Run | `conforms` | Target classes matched | Focus nodes | Results |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Deleted shapes, corpus as published | True | 0/34 | 0 | 0 |
| Deleted shapes, corpus with the generated binding | False | 23/34 | 228 | 287 |
| Generated shapes, corpus with the generated binding | False | 24/24 | 191 | 316 |

The first row is a clean pass that means nothing. Not one shape selected a single node, so every constraint held vacuously. Restoring the file on its own would reproduce exactly that result.

The second row is the finding. The same shapes, unchanged, over the same examples, unchanged, once the JSON has an RDF interpretation: 228 focus nodes and 287 violations. The shapes that were deleted were not stale or wrong. They were pointed at a graph that did not exist.

## 7. Two engines, one disagreement

Every SHACL figure above is pySHACL. The same shapes and data were also run through the Open Ontologies Rust engine as an independent check. The two agree exactly on reach and disagree on findings:

| Measure | pySHACL | Open Ontologies |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Focus nodes selected | 191 | 191 |
| `sh:class` results | 165 | 0 |
| `sh:nodeKind` results | 122 | 0 |
| `sh:maxCount` results | 27 | 27 |
| `sh:datatype` results | 2 | 8 |

The disagreement is recorded rather than resolved in favour of the convenient answer, and both gaps are ours. The Open Ontologies engine evaluates neither `sh:class` nor `sh:nodeKind`, so 287 of pySHACL's 316 findings (165 class, 122 nodeKind) are invisible to it. It also rejects a literal carrying exactly the required datatype when that datatype is a derived numeric type: `"1024"^^xsd:nonNegativeInteger` fails `sh:datatype xsd:nonNegativeInteger` while `xsd:integer`, `xsd:decimal` and `xsd:string` all pass. Both are queued as defects against our own engine; the eight-line repro is in `tests/test_engine_findings.py`.

A third defect belongs to rdflib. The single processor error in the first table is `jsonschema/examples/Identifier/good/minimal_string_example.json`, whose entire content is the JSON document `"dataset-12345"`. Expanding a scalar JSON-LD document yields an empty array, so an empty graph is the correct outcome; rdflib 7.6.0 raises `UnboundLocalError` from `plugins/parsers/jsonld.py:242`, because `parse` handles `list` and `dict` and leaves `resources` unassigned for anything else. Adding a context masks it, which is why the error count falls to zero in rows two and three rather than the file being fixed.

## 8. Namespace corrections

The prefix map is taken from the only context DCAT-US has published. Three entries are changed, each recorded in `namespaces.json` with its evidence:

| Prefix | As published | Used here | Why |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `dcat-us` | `http://data.resources.gov/ontology/dcat-us#` | `http://resources.data.gov/ontology/dcat-us#` | `data.resources.gov` does not resolve; the host is transposed |
| `dcat-us-shp` | `http://data.resources.gov/shapes/dcat-us#` | `http://resources.data.gov/shapes/dcat-us#` | same transposition |
| `org` | `http://www.w3c.org/ns/org#` | `http://www.w3.org/ns/org#` | the Organization Ontology declares `w3.org`; `w3c.org` redirects in a browser but mints different IRIs |

`dc` and `xsd` are added because the schema uses `dc:publisher` and several `xsd` datatypes that the published context never declared.

## 9. Reproducing this

```sh
git clone https://github.com/GSA/dcat-us.git upstream
git -C upstream checkout 7a6e803
pip install -e '.[dev]'
make build            # regenerates build/ and this report
make test             # asserts every headline figure
```
